title: Rotate the Playlist
statement: A music app shows a playlist as an array of song IDs. The "rotate" button moves the last song to the front, and pressing it k times does that k times. Return the playlist after k presses as a new array. k can be larger than the playlist length.

answerKey.pattern: Index arithmetic with modulo: the song at index i moves to index (i + k) % n
keyPoints: Return an empty array when the playlist is empty, before using % n
Reduce k with k % n, because n presses bring the playlist back to where it started
Create a result array of length n and put songs[i] at index (i + k) % n
edgeCases: k equal to the length returns the same order
k much larger than the length
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Move the last song to the front k times: O(n · k), too slow when k is large
Reverse the whole array, then reverse the two parts: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, an equally good answer

hints: Pressing the button n times (n = number of songs) gives back the original playlist. What does that tell you about a huge k?
After the rotation, where does the song at index i end up? Try it on [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with k = 2.
It ends up at index (i + k) % n. Fill a new array using that formula, and handle n = 0 first so you never divide by zero.
